correctness.rationale: For a triangular block map T, im(T)∩U=im(A)+B(ker D) inside the preserved subspace U. A regularity witness S must lift im(T)∩U through A. Conversely, if im(T)∩U=im(A), take preimages in U for a basis of the intersection, arbitrary T-preimages for a basis extending it in im(T), then extend S to preserve U by using a basis adapted to U and im(T). Thus regularity is precisely vanishing of the independent restriction/projection B↦(ker D→coker A). The map on B is onto (lift a basis of the cokernel and extend the kernel basis), so its zero fiber has q^(ab−ij) elements. The count of rank r comes from the product of two full-rank rectangular counts divided by |GL_r|, giving the stated p and the exact joint law under uniform sampling. For the limit, 0≤Φ_t−Φ_∞≤∑_{h>t}q^(−h); the finite/limit mass ratio differs from 1 by O_q(q^(−n+k)) for k≤n. Since ∑_k q^k π_q(k)<∞, this bounds the total error including the k>n tail by O_q(q^(−n)). Product, restricted weighting, and normalization (denominator ≥Φ_∞) give the claimed uniform two-block rate. For i₂>i₁ the conditional expectations differ by Cov(g(J),q^(−(i₂−i₁)J))/E[q^(−(i₂−i₁)J)] evaluated at i₁; the covariance is strictly negative for nonconstant nondecreasing g by the independent-pair identity. Apply the identity again to f and the decreasing conditional expectation. Supports are full for all admissible defects, and the same proof holds in the limit with the stipulated integrability. L_q<1 because the pair (1,1) has positive unweighted mass and receives weight <1. Numerical replay at q=2: use 60 product factors and sum i,j=0,…,15, obtaining approximately 0.6998513223055354; product tails are bounded by 2^(−60), omitted masses by 4∑_{k≥16}2^(−k²) per coordinate (Φ_∞>1/4). This was a floating-point corroboration, not a proof of the law. Read checks/check_parabolic_regular.py and the frozen 6574-matrix output, including 163 witness searches; the checker is prime-field only and was not rerun.
